texts.preamble: Pooja Bakshi vs The State on 29 May, 2025 Dlst010070202025 In The Court Of Shri Sunil Gupta Additional Sessions Judge-6, South District Saket Courts, New Delhi Revision Petition No. 246/2025 In The Matter Of: Ms. Pooja Bakshi W/o Sh. Manish Bakshi R/o Property No. 403, Ward No.3, Mehrauli, New Delhi-110030. ............ Revisi Versus 1. The State Government of N.C.T. of Delhi, New Secretariat, I.P. Estate, New Delhi (Through its Chief Secretary) 2 . Sh. Devender Sejwal S/o Sh. Badle Ram, R/o F-322, Lado Sarai, New Delhi-110030 ......... Responden Instituted on : 24.05.2025 Reserved on : 24.05.2025 Pronounced on : 29.05.2025 Judgment
texts.facts: A complaint U/s 138 NI Act was filed by respondent no.2 Devender Sejwal (hereinafter referred to as respondent only) against the revisionist which came to be Pooja Bakshi vs The State on 29 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137708841/ 1 listed before Ld. Magistrate on 04.07.2023. Cognizance was taken thereupon on 03.01.2024 and revisionist was summoned as an accused on the same day. On the next date of hearing i.e., 30.03.2024, one Counsel appeared on her behalf and filed memo of appearance whereas accused had remained absent. An application for exemption from personal appearance was moved on her behalf which was allowed subject to cost of Rs. 3000/- to be paid to the complainant on NDOH i.e., 10.05.2024. On 10.05.2024, revisionist was present alongwith her Counsel and fresh vakalatnama was filed on her behalf. She was admitted to bail on furnishing bail bond in the sum of Rs. 25,000/- with one surety in the like amount but the bond was not furnished which was directed to be furnished within 3 days. An application seeking waiver of cost imposed vide order dated 30.03.2024 moved on her behalf was disposed of by reducing the cost to Rs. 1500/-. Notice u/s 251 Cr.P.C. pertaining to substance of accusations against the revisionist was served upon her. Both these orders are being challenged by way of present revision petition. It has been argued by Ld. Counsel for revisionist that he had earlier also filed a revision petition which was disposed of vide order dated 28.04.2025 of Ld. ASJ-05 (South) on a technical ground and liberty was granted to him to file the same afresh. It has been submitted that the order dated 10.05.2024 passed by Ld. MM-01 (South), NI Act was not sustainable in the eyes of law. It has been submitted that the revisionist was appearing before the Court on that day for the first time. She was even not having the copy of documents i.e., copy of complaint filed by the respondent and documents being relied upon. 2 5. Notice of the revision petition was not issued to respondent Devender Sejwal as the revision petition is liable to be dismissed for the reasons mentioned hereinafter. The Court has also not gone into the issue of maintainability of present revision petition alongwith that of limitation for the same reason. 6. Relevant portion of the impugned order is being reproduced below for ready reference:- SUNIL by SUNIL GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.05.30 15:26:02 +0530 "Substance of accusation/notice u/s 251 CrPC has been served upon the accused and explained to her. The case of the complainant and the allegations against her were explained to the accused in Hindi and the consequences of pleading guilty and the punishment provided for the alleged offence was also explained to her. The details of the offence alleged against her was also explained to the accused. The documents on record were also shown to the accused and she has pleaded guilty, after understanding the alleged offence and the consequences that may follow. The accused also admitted receipt of the loan and she sought time to repay the same in installments. Upon specific query of the Court regarding whether or not she has to say anything else, she stated that she does not want to say anything else apart from seeking time to repay. In view of her plea of guilt and as per the process prescribed u/s 251 read with Section 252 CrPC, accused is hereby convicted for the offence punishable under Section 138 NI Act." 7.
texts.arguments: It has been submitted that she was not prepared to answer the questions put to her by Ld. Magistrate as she was not given sufficient time to take advise from her Counsel. It has been submitted that she was having a valid defence however she was not given a fair opportunity to disclose the same. It has been submitted that part payment to the tune of Rs. 1,35,000/- had already been made to the respondent from time to time so only a sum of Rs. 1,65,000/- was remaining to be paid to him. It has been submitted that Ld. Magistrate should not have convicted the revisionist only because she had pleaded guilty. He has relied upon the following judgments:- a. Satish Vs. Food Safety Officer, Criminal OP(MD) No. 10665/2023(Madras High Court); b. Thippaswamy Vs. State of Karnataka, AIR 1983 SC747. In the landmark judgement titled as Indian Bank Association & Ors. Vs. Union of India & Anr. Writ Petition (Civil) No. 18/2013, Hon'ble Apex Court had issued following directions for speedy trial of cases u/s 138 NI Act:- "21. 12. Similarly, the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Thippaswamy Vs. State of Karnataka (Supra) is also distinguishable on facts.
